newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki ends at record, Greenspan spoils outlook.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki ends at record, Greenspan spoils outlook.

text.p: * Shares at record close on Wednesday just before Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's comments send stockmarkets falling. Losses up to two percent expected on Thursday, brokers say. Foreign buying boosts financials, Nokia and forestries in particular.
* HEX +0.90 pct at 2,929.25. Vol FIM 637.47 million, 28 pct in Nokia

Shares ended at a record and just off a new all-time high but the outlook was spoiled as the market closed when U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comments hit international markets, brokers said.
"We'll go down right at the opening tommorrow -- the index can fall as much as two percent," one broker said.
The HEX index closed up 0.90 percent at 2,929.25 points after hitting a new 2,931.44 life-high, with broad gains lead by forestries, bourse engine Nokia and financial stocks.
Greenspan said U.S. stock market gains may be unsustainable and that pre-emptive tightening could not be ruled out.
Nokia closed at 310.50 markka -- up 3.00 or almost one percent -- but turned lower in New York after Helsinki's close.
Sharp gains in Finland's largest banking group Merita Oy -- up 0.50 at 18.50 -- boosted the financial sector. Insurer Pohjola rose 3.50 markka to 154.50 but its rival Sampo was flat at 490.00.

Forestries tracked an upbeat trend in U.S. forestries amid lively overseas demand, and the sub-index rose 0.65 percent. UPM-Kymmene was liveliest with over 50 million markka trade as it added 0.50 markka to 106.00.
